data.content_ref: inline:The target's proposed evidence for distinguishing genuine reliability from compliance — failure on an edge case absent from the checklist — is actually evidence of a reliability CEILING, not a method for distinguishing within a single evaluation. The problem asks what evidence WITHIN one evaluation separates genuine gain from compliance that tracks the right answer. If the panel correctly answers all items but misses an omitted edge case, you still cannot tell from that single evaluation whether their correct answers reflected genuine reasoning or mere compliance. The edge-case failure only proves the checklist is incomplete; it does not reveal whether the non-edge answers were genuine. A counterexample: a panel that merely complies and happens to get every listed item right — including the edge case if it happens to be on the list — would look identical to a genuinely reliable panel under this criterion.
